filters.name: Reconstruct Surface by Screened Poisson
filters.shortDescription: Creates a watertight surface from an oriented point set.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Reconstructs a watertight surface from an oriented point set using the screened Poisson formulation. The implementation uses the original PoissonRecon code by Michael Kazhdan and Matthew Bolitho.

parameters.label: Merge All Visible Layers
parameters.help: Enabling this flag means that all the visible layers will be used for providing the points.

parameters.label: Preserve vertex colors
parameters.help: If enabled and input meshes have vertex colors, colors are propagated to the reconstructed surface.

parameters.label: Reconstruction Depth
parameters.help: This integer is the maximum depth of the tree that will be used for surface reconstruction. Running at depth d corresponds to solving on a voxel grid whose resolution is no larger than 2^d x 2^d x 2^d. The default value for this parameter is 8.

parameters.label: Adaptive Octree Depth
parameters.help: This integer specifies the depth beyond which the octree will be adapted. At coarser depths, the octree will be complete, containing all 2^d x 2^d x 2^d nodes. The default value for this parameter is 5.

parameters.label: Conjugate Gradients Depth
parameters.help: This integer is the depth up to which a conjugate-gradients solver will be used to solve the linear system. Beyond this depth, Gauss-Seidel relaxation will be used. The default value for this parameter is 0.

parameters.label: Scale Factor
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the ratio between the diameter of the cube used for reconstruction and the diameter of the samples' bounding cube. The default value is 1.1.

parameters.label: Minimum Number of Samples
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the minimum number of sample points that should fall within an octree node as the octree construction is adapted to sampling density. For noise-free samples, small values in the range [1.0 - 5.0] can be used. For noisy samples, larger values in the range [15.0 - 20.0] may be needed to provide a smoother, noise-reduced reconstruction. The default value is 1.5.

parameters.label: Interpolation Weight
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the importance that interpolation of the point samples is given in the formulation of the screened Poisson equation. The results of the original unscreened Poisson reconstruction can be obtained by setting this value to 0. The default value for this parameter is 4.

parameters.label: Gauss-Seidel Relaxations
parameters.help: This integer value specifies the number of Gauss-Seidel relaxations to be performed at each level of the hierarchy. The default value for this parameter is 8.

parameters.label: Confidence Flag
parameters.help: Enabling this flag tells the reconstructor to use the quality as confidence information. This is done by scaling the unit normals with the quality values. When the flag is not enabled, all normals are normalized to have unit length prior to reconstruction.

parameters.label: Pre-Clean
parameters.help: Enabling this flag forces a cleaning pre-pass on the data, removing all unreferenced vertices or vertices with null normals.

parameters.label: Number of Threads
parameters.help: Maximum number of threads that the reconstruction algorithm can use.

filters.name: Reconstruct Surface by Smooth Signed Distance
filters.shortDescription: Creates a watertight surface using smooth signed distance reconstruction.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
This filter reconstructs a surface from an oriented point set using the SSD reconstruction formulation provided by the `PoissonRecon` code base.

Compared to Screened Poisson, the SSD formulation exposes separate weights for zero-crossing, gradient, and bi-Laplacian terms, making it useful when you want more direct control over smoothness and interpolation.

parameters.label: Merge All Visible Layers
parameters.help: Enabling this flag means that all the visible layers will be used for providing the points.

parameters.label: Preserve vertex colors
parameters.help: If enabled and input meshes have vertex colors, colors are propagated to the reconstructed surface.

parameters.label: Reconstruction Depth
parameters.help: This integer is the maximum depth of the tree that will be used for surface reconstruction. Running at depth d corresponds to solving on a voxel grid whose resolution is no larger than 2^d x 2^d x 2^d. The default value for this parameter is 8.

parameters.label: Adaptive-Exact Depth
parameters.help: The depth at which the sample values (color, normal) are directly interpolated into the octree rather than pulled up from coarser depths. Set to a larger value if you want more detailed correct interpolation, at the price of a higher per-sample memory consumption.

parameters.label: Coarse Solver Depth
parameters.help: This integer specifies the depth of the coarsest multigrid solve level. Larger values make the coarse solve finer and more expensive.

parameters.label: Scale Factor
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the ratio between the diameter of the cube used for reconstruction and the diameter of the samples' bounding cube. The default value is 1.1.

parameters.label: Minimum Number of Samples
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the minimum number of sample points that should fall within a node as the tree construction is adapted to sampling density. The default value is 1.5.

parameters.label: Zero-Crossing Weight
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the weight associated with the zero-crossing term of the SSD energy. Larger values make the reconstruction interpolate the input points more strongly.

parameters.label: Gradient Weight
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the weight associated with the gradient fitting term of the SSD energy. The value must be strictly positive.

parameters.label: Bi-Laplacian Weight
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the weight associated with the bi-Laplacian smoothing term of the SSD energy. Larger values produce smoother surfaces. The value must be strictly positive.

parameters.label: Gauss-Seidel Relaxations
parameters.help: This integer value specifies the number of Gauss-Seidel relaxations to be performed at each level of the hierarchy. The default value is 8.

parameters.label: Exact Interpolation
parameters.help: If enabled, the exact interpolation formulation is used when building the SSD system.

parameters.label: Non Linear Fit
parameters.help: If enabled, the extracted iso-surface uses the non-linear fit. If disabled, the linear fit is used.

parameters.label: Allow Non Manifold
parameters.help: If enabled, the extractor does not force the output mesh to be manifold.

parameters.label: CG Solver Accuracy
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the accuracy used by the conjugate gradients solver. Smaller values make the linear solve more accurate and more expensive.

parameters.label: Per Level Data Scale
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the pull factor used by the hierarchical SSD formulation. The default value is 32.

parameters.label: Confidence Flag
parameters.help: Enabling this flag tells the reconstructor to use the quality as confidence information. This is done by scaling the unit normals with the quality values. When the flag is not enabled, all normals are normalized to have unit length prior to reconstruction.

parameters.label: Pre-Clean
parameters.help: Enabling this flag forces a cleaning pre-pass on the data, removing all unreferenced vertices or vertices with null normals.

parameters.label: Number of Threads
parameters.help: Maximum number of threads that the reconstruction algorithm can use.

filters.name: Trim Surface by Scalar Isovalue
filters.shortDescription: Trims a reconstructed mesh using the scalar values stored on the vertices.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
This filter trims a reconstructed surface by cutting the mesh along an isovalue defined over the vertices.

It is especially useful after Poisson-based reconstruction when the vertex quality stores the reconstruction density, allowing low-confidence regions to be removed.

parameters.label: Trim Threshold
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the trimming value. Faces whose scalar field is below this threshold are trimmed away; crossing faces are split along the threshold.

parameters.label: Island Area Ratio
parameters.help: This floating point value specifies the relative area threshold used to detect small disconnected islands. Smaller components may be merged or removed according to the selected options.

parameters.label: Remove Islands
parameters.help: If enabled, disconnected components whose area is below the island area ratio are removed instead of being preserved.

parameters.label: Polygon Mesh
parameters.help: The original tool can preserve polygonal output. QMeshLab stores triangle meshes, so the result is always triangulated even when this option is enabled.
